title: The Mirror in the Attic
summary: Leo finds a strange mirror in the attic of his new house.
coverScene: A lonely, dust-covered antique mirror stands in the center of a dark attic, reflecting the empty room behind it while the silhouette of a man stands frozen in the glass.

sentences.text: Leo moves into a new house.
The house is very old.
It is a cold night.
Leo is alone.
The house is quiet.
Leo walks to the attic.
The attic is dark.
It smells like dust.
He finds a big mirror.
It is in the corner.
Leo walks to the mirror.
He looks at his face.
The glass is very clear.
He moves his head.
His reflection does not move.
The man in the mirror stands still.
He stares at Leo.
Leo feels a great fear.
He wants to leave now.
He turns around.
He walks to the door.
His heart beats fast.
He feels eyes on his back.
He does not look back.
Leo closes the heavy door.
He locks the door tight.
He looks through the keyhole.
He sees the mirror.
The reflection is still there.
It watches the door.
It has a hungry look.

He decided to explore the attic after he finished unpacking his boxes.
The space was dark and smelled of dust, but he found a beautiful mirror standing in the corner.
Leo walked toward the mirror to look at his face.
He noticed that the glass was very clear, although it was covered in age and dirt.
When he moved his head to the left, his reflection did not move at all.
He stood still as he watched the man in the mirror staring back at him.
If he had been a brave man, he might have stayed there to see what happened.
However, Leo felt a great fear and decided that he should leave the room immediately.
He turned around and walked toward the attic door while his heart beat fast.
He did not look back, but he could feel the eyes of the reflection on his back.
Leo closed the heavy door and locked it tight behind him.
He wanted to be sure that nothing could follow him out of that dark attic.

sentences.text: Leo arrived at the old house on a cold autumn evening, the wind rattling the loose shutters like distant applause.
The building loomed, its timber bones creaking under the weight of forgotten years, and an uneasy silence settled in every empty hallway.
Leo had heard rumors of the house's long history, yet none of them prepared him for the chill that seemed to seep from the very walls.
He placed his suitcase on the worn front step, feeling the floorboards groan beneath his weight as if the house were inhaling.
A faint smell of damp pine and old paper hung in the air, hinting at stories that had never been spoken aloud.
After hours of shuffling boxes and arranging furniture, Leo finally felt the living room take shape, its dim lamps casting amber pools on the faded carpet.
The house, still echoing with the soft sighs of settling timber, seemed to reward his effort with a tentative calm.
Curiosity, however, pressed against his chest like a persistent drumbeat, urging him toward the narrow staircase that vanished into darkness.
He remembered the attic, spoken of in hushed tones by the previous tenant, as a place where dust whispered and secrets lingered.
With a tentative breath, he pulled the attic door open, the hinges protesting with a long, metallic sigh.
The attic greeted him with a thick, stale darkness that seemed to swallow the weak beam of his flashlight.
Cobwebs hung from the low ceiling like delicate curtains, and the floor was a patchwork of uneven boards that creaked under each cautious step.
A sour, metallic odor rose from piles of forgotten belongings, mingling with the faint perfume of old wood and long-forgotten incense.
Among the clutter, a tall, ornate mirror stood in the far corner, its frame gilded with tarnished leaves that caught the trembling light.
It seemed out of place, as if a portal had been dropped into the attic by accident, inviting a hesitant gaze.
Leo approached the glass, his breath fogging the surface momentarily before the surrounding dust settled like a thin veil.
Despite the grime that clung to its edges, the mirror's surface was startlingly clear, reflecting the attic with a precision that defied its age.
His own silhouette appeared, framed by the faint glow of the flashlight, yet the image seemed unnervingly crisp, as if the glass were a window rather than a pane.
He lifted his right hand, watching the reflection mimic the motion with perfect fidelity, each finger articulated like a puppet obeying an unseen puppeteer.
A sudden, inexplicable chill ran down his spine, and for an instant he wondered whether the mirror might be more than mere glass.
When Leo turned his head to the left, expecting his reflection to follow, the image remained stubbornly still, its eyes fixed on his own.
The silence in the attic seemed to thicken, each breath he drew echoing louder than the last, as if the room itself were holding its breath.
He stared back at the fixed figure, feeling the uncanny sensation that the mirror was watching him, not merely reflecting him.
A thin line of doubt crept along his spine, whispering that the stillness was a warning, a silent command to remain unmoving.
Yet the urge to understand, to test the boundary between reality and illusion, tugged at his curiosity like a moth to flame.
If bravery had taken root in his heart, he might have lingered, daring the mirror to reveal its secret.
Instead, a surge of primal fear rose, hot and sudden, flooding his thoughts with images of unseen eyes and silent predators.
He imagined the reflection stepping out, its cold stare carving a path through the thin veil that separated worlds.
A shiver ran along his arms, and the notion of staying any longer felt like an invitation to danger.
With a breath that tasted of iron, Leo made the decisive choice to retreat, his feet moving before his mind could protest.
He spun on his heel, the flashlight flickering as if hesitant to follow his sudden departure.
Each step toward the attic door resonated like a drumbeat against the wooden planks, amplifying the rapid thud of his own heart.
He could not shake the sensation that unseen eyes lingered behind him, their gaze lingering on his back as if measuring his resolve.
The attic seemed to close in, the shadows deepening, while the faint echo of his own breathing filled the cramped space.
Yet he forced himself forward, each breath a visible puff of vapor, his determination a thin thread against the looming dread.
Reaching the heavy oak door, Leo grasped the tarnished knob, feeling the cold metal seep into his palm.
He pulled it shut with a weighty thud that resonated through the attic, as if the house itself exhaled a sigh of relief.
The lock clicked into place, its metallic sound echoing like a promise that nothing could follow him out of that darkness.
He pressed his palm against the wood, feeling the vibrations of his own heartbeat travel through the grain.
A thin veil of safety settled over him, though the lingering presence in the attic made the air feel heavy with unspoken warning.
Leo knelt before the door, aligning his eye with the narrow keyhole, and peered into the dim interior.
The flashlight's beam, now a thin line, illuminated the mirror's surface, revealing the stubborn figure still poised within.
Its reflection stared back, eyes cold and hungry, as if the glass had become a portal to a waiting predator.
A ripple of dread spread through Leo's chest, the sensation of being observed intensifying with each silent second.
He realized that the mirror's gaze was not a mere reflection but a sentient stare that might reach beyond the glass at any moment.
Without daring another glance, he turned away, the weight of the locked door anchoring his resolve like a fragile shield.
The attic's darkness seemed to pulse, each shadow whispering a promise that the mirror would wait for his return.
Outside, the wind howled louder, rattling the shutters and reminding Leo that the world beyond still moved, indifferent to his terror.
He descended the staircase, each step echoing a final farewell to the unseen watcher that lingered above.
Yet, as the house settled behind him, a faint glimmer caught his eye from the attic window, a reminder that some mirrors never truly close.
